name: Question 19
problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
G=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}+2 & \,\,-2 \\ 2 & \,\,\sqrt{3}-2\end{aligned}],\,\,\,J=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & \,1 \\ 0 & \,\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $G=PJ{P}^{-1},$ find $12\operatorname{arctan}⁡G.$
worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)=12\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and the given matrix $G,$ we have

$$
12\operatorname{arctan}⁡G=12\operatorname{arctan}⁡(PJ{P}^{-1})=P\cdot (12\operatorname{arctan}⁡J)\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $J$ is a Jordan block with $\sqrt{3}$ on the main diagonal, we have

$$
f(J)=[\begin{aligned}f(\sqrt{3}) & {f}^{′}(\sqrt{3}) \\ 0 & f(\sqrt{3})\end{aligned}].
$$

The derivative of $f$ is ${f}^{′}(x)=\frac{12}{{x}^{2}+1}$ So, we get

$$
12\operatorname{arctan}⁡J=[\begin{aligned}f(\sqrt{3}) & {f}^{′}(\sqrt{3}) \\ 0 & f(\sqrt{3})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4\pi  & 3 \\ 0 & 4\pi \end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1\cdot 2-2\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}12\operatorname{arctan}⁡G & =P\cdot (12\operatorname{arctan}⁡J)\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4\pi  & 3 \\ 0 & 4\pi \end{aligned}]\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2\pi +3 & 4\pi -3 \\ 4\pi  & -4\pi \end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4\pi +6 & -6 \\ 6 & 4\pi -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the following matrices:

G=[3+2−223−2],J=[3103],P=[2221]

Given that G=PJP−1, find 12arctan⁡G.

a
[4π−6−334π+6]
b
[2π+3−662π−3]
c
[2π+63−32π−6]
d
[4π+6−664π−6]
e
[4π−3−664π+3]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Given a function f and matrices A and S, where S is invertible, we have f(SAS−1)=S⋅f(A)⋅S−1.

For f(x)=12arctan⁡x and the given matrix G, we have

12arctan⁡G=12arctan⁡(PJP−1)=P⋅(12arctan⁡J)⋅P−1.

Now, since J is a Jordan block with 3 on the main diagonal, we have

f(J)=[f(3)f′(3)0f(3)].

The derivative of f is f′(x)=12x2+1 So, we get

12arctan⁡J=[f(3)f′(3)0f(3)]=[4π304π].

Also, the inverse of P is

P−1=11⋅2−2⋅2[1−2−22]=12[−122−2].

Therefore, we conclude that

12arctan⁡G=P⋅(12arctan⁡J)⋅P−1=[2221][4π304π]12[−122−2]=[2221][−2π+34π−34π−4π]=[4π+6−664π−6].
